The payment period of 90 days deviates from the preferred Net 45 and fallback Net 30 terms, and the clause fails to provide the required right to withhold disputed amounts in good faith.
findings.sourceSpan: within ninety (90) days of the date of receipt of the invoice

findings.deviationReason: The 8% monthly late fee substantially breaches the fallback position, which caps late interest at 1% per month.
findings.sourceSpan: interest at a rate of 8% per month

findings.deviationReason: The clause assigns all deliverable IP exclusively to the Supplier without providing the Customer the required exclusive, perpetual, irrevocable licence under the fallback position.
findings.sourceSpan: shall remain the exclusive property of the Supplier.

findings.deviationReason: The clause grants the Supplier a perpetual, irrevocable licence to use Customer data for any purpose, breaching the requirement that the Customer retains ownership of its data.
findings.sourceSpan:
The Customer grants the Supplier a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide licence to use the
Customer's data for any purpose.

findings.deviationReason: The confidentiality obligation lasts for only one year from disclosure, breaching the fallback requirement of at least three years of survival post-termination.
findings.sourceSpan:
Each party shall keep the other party's Confidential Information confidential for a period of one (1)
year from disclosure.

findings.deviationReason: The clause allows data processing in any country without instruction and specifies a 30-day breach notification period, which violates the 72-hour notice fallback.
findings.sourceSpan:
The Supplier may process personal data of the Customer in any country and shall notify the
Customer of any data breach within thirty (30) days of discovery.

findings.deviationReason: The indemnity is one-sided against the Customer for all losses, contrary to the playbook requirement for mutual indemnities limited to third-party claims.
findings.sourceSpan:
The Customer shall indemnify the Supplier against all losses, liabilities, damages and costs
arising out of or in connection with this Agreement.

findings.deviationReason: Unlimited liability is restricted to gross negligence, failing to include required carve-outs such as fraud, wilful misconduct, and confidentiality breaches.
findings.sourceSpan:
The Supplier's liability under or in connection with this Agreement shall be unlimited in respect of
the Customer's claims only where caused by gross negligence.

findings.deviationReason: The Customer's liability is unlimited, breaching the requirement that each party's aggregate liability must be capped at a fixed multiple of fees.
findings.sourceSpan: The Customer's liability to the Supplier under this Agreement shall be unlimited.

findings.deviationReason: The exclusion of consequential damages is one-sided in favour of the Supplier without reciprocal limitation of the Customer's exposure, failing the fallback requirement.
findings.sourceSpan: The Supplier shall not be liable for any loss of profit, loss of revenue or loss of data.

findings.deviationReason: The clause binds the Customer to five-year terms with twelve months' notice to prevent auto-renewal, entirely lacking a termination for convenience right on 30 or 90 days' notice.
findings.sourceSpan:
This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and continue for an initial term of five (5)

years, automatically renewing for successive five-year terms unless terminated on twelve (12)
months' notice.

findings.deviationReason: The clause completely denies the Customer the right to terminate for convenience, breaching the mandatory requirement and fallback.
findings.sourceSpan:
The
Customer may not terminate for convenience.

findings.deviationReason: The clause specifies Delaware law and court jurisdiction rather than the preferred customer home jurisdiction or the fallback neutral options (England and Wales or New York with arbitration).
findings.sourceSpan:
laws of the State of

findings.deviationReason: No matching playbook rule

Missing clause: nothing in this document addresses "IP infringement indemnity". The supplier must defend and indemnify the customer against third-party claims that the services or deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.

Missing clause: nothing in this document addresses "Termination for cause and cure period". Either party may terminate for material breach that remains uncured 30 days after written notice, or immediately upon insolvency.

Missing clause: nothing in this document addresses "Fee increases and price protection". The supplier may not increase fees during the initial term, and later increases must be capped (for example CPI or 5%) with at least 60 days' notice.

Missing clause: nothing in this document addresses "Service levels and remedies". The supplier must meet defined uptime and support response commitments, with service credits and a termination right for repeated failure.
